title: Dynamic quant fallback loop and op-fingerprint detection plan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After deploying the dynamic quant fallback feature that automatically routes unsupported kernels to float execution, several production models entered a degraded state: intermittent crash loops on specific sequences and silent accuracy drift for longer-context prompts. This ticket coordinates a short-term mitigation, a stability hotfix, and a longer-term detection and prevention plan focused on op fingerprinting, kernel selection determinism, and observability.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a spike in 5xx errors and quality regressions for a subset of customers using int8 quant variants. Root cause preliminary analysis pointed to a mismatch between the op fingerprint used to decide fallback and the runtime kernel signature (scale/order differences), which caused the fallback path to run with incompatible dequant semantics in some batched scenarios. The fallback loop was amplified by autoscaler behavior that repeatedly cycled pods with partial KV cache state, producing transient but recurring failures.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC - Alert: increased 5xx rate and token-level perplexity drift from canary evals (Grafana).
2026-03-09 02:40 UTC - Initial mitigation: toggled feature flag dynamic_quant_fallback=false for affected model group to stop new fallbacks.
2026-03-09 04:00 UTC - Emergency rollback of runtime rollout to runtime-1.21 for high traffic zones.
2026-03-09 08:30 UTC - Hotfix PR created (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124) to add stricter kernel signature checks and safe-conversion gate.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Hotfix deployed to canary and validated against golden-output suite; no regressions observed on canary models.
2026-03-11 15:20 UTC - Started longer-term follow-ups: op fingerprint redesign, CI gating, and telemetry improvements assigned.
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - This ticket created to centralize follow-ups and owners.
2026-03-14 12:00 UTC - Post-deploy monitoring shows fallback-rate stabilized but op-fingerprint mismatch alerts remain elevated for a small fraction of model conversions.
root_cause: Multiple interacting causes: 1) the op fingerprinting heuristic produced false positives for fused ops created by the new converter path; 2) the fallback execution path assumed a dequantization ordering that differed from the quantized kernel in batched merges, producing silent numerical drift; 3) autoscaler churn combined with partial KV cache warmup created a pod eviction spiral that amplified the surface area of the incompatibility.
steps_taken: Disabled dynamic quant fallback globally for affected model families (feature flag).
Rolled back the runtime rollout in high-traffic regions to runtime-1.21 to restore stable kernel selection.
Merged emergency hotfix PR that adds explicit kernel signature validation and aborts fallback when signatures differ (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124).
Added a temporary rate-limit on converter-driven model uploads to allow staged verification.
Ran a targeted eval suite across 200 representative prompts to quantify drift and confirm rollback effectiveness.

On-call - Maintain feature flag readiness and escalate if fallback_rate > 0.5% for 30m (ongoing)
qa_plan: Add unit tests that assert exact numerical equivalence (within epsilon) between quantized kernel output and fallback float execution for fused ops.
Create end-to-end canary harness that replays production request traces into canaries with KV cache warmup simulation.
Add randomized stress tests that exercise autoscaler churn with partial KV caches to reproduce the eviction spiral locally.
rollout_plan: Staged re-enable pathway: 1) close all failing conversion paths behind opt-in flag; 2) land deterministic op fingerprinting and kernel-signature checks; 3) enable canary runs for 24h with golden-output gating and drift < 0.2% on eval prompts; 4) progressively enable across regions with monitoring guardrails and automatic rollback on alert triggers.
monitoring_upgrades: New Grafana panel showing fallback_rate by model_family and op_fingerprint (panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant/fallback-rate?panelId=7).
Alert: fallback_rate > 0.3% for 15m AND golden_eval_drift > 0.2% triggers automated feature-flag rollback.
Histogram of op fingerprint collisions and a counter for signature-mismatch aborts.
KV cache warmup metric and eviction_count metric to correlate with crash loops.
review_comments: PM (Jon Park): Prioritize stable rollout for top-10 paying customers; consider temporary credits for impacted customers.
Infra (Priya Nair): Autoscaler tuning required — we should add pod grace periods when converter-backed models are uploading.
Research (Dr. Emma Li): Evaluate whether quantization converter should emit canonical lowered ops to avoid fused-op ambiguities.
notes: Do not re-run mass converter jobs until op-fingerprint schema is stable — we observed conversions that changed fused-op boundaries.
Consider coupling converter output with a signed manifest containing kernel-signature metadata for on-deploy verification.
